conviction_note: Q3 is largely pre-guided (79% of days booked at $113,681/day as of 1 Sep) and implies EPS around NOK 8.1 against a single stale Yahoo estimate of NOK 7.36, and the Q4-to-date booking update should be a record. But the peers have already shown the sector's Q4 bookings (Frontline Suezmax spot $324,300 at 69%, Okeanis $410,900 at 60%), and when they did their stocks moved -1.9% to +2.1%. So the lean is mild: p_up 56 on a 5% move gives +0.6. The findings sum (+0.6) happens to match that, and neither number was fitted to the other.

findings.finding: The company's own Q3 booking guide (79% of 1,304 fleet days at $113,681/day, Suezmax at $130,239) implies Q3 EPS of about $0.87 (NOK 8.1 at the September USD/NOK of 9.3), even if the open 21% earned only the booked rate. That is about 10% above the single Yahoo estimate of NOK 7.36.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 beat Yahoo's estimate by 47% and the stock moved -0.63%; Q2 matched and it moved -1.39% (baseline history, observed NewsWeb dates). Beats have not been bought, on n=2.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the guide is public and anyone modelling the name can derive this. What remains unpriced is only the gap to a single stale Yahoo estimate. If the market had held a higher bar, that estimate would have been revised up more than 0.5% since the guide; it moved 7.32 to 7.36. Sized near zero because it lands inside what the company guided.
findings.independence: Q3 operating cash generation looks strong: per the main-list prospectus, cash at 30 Sep 2026 ($356.3m) was flat on 30 Jun ($356.7m) despite a $43.3m dividend and three deliveries (https://www.capitaltankers.com/files/pdf/CAPITAL_TANKERS_CORP_Prospectus.pdf). Debt also rose $175m, so this is weak.

findings.finding: The Q4-to-date booking update should be a record and far above the stale Yahoo Q4 EPS of NOK 5.73 (range 3.53-7.94), which sits BELOW the Q3 estimate. Frontline's 20 Nov release shows Q4 contracted Suezmax spot at $324,300/day (69%) and LR2/Aframax at $190,800 (68%), against Q3 achieved of $102,500 and $67,800. CAPT's fleet is 8 Suezmax and 8 Aframax/LR2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CAPT's Q2 booking update (Q3 79% at $113.7k, about flat on Q2's $116.3k) was met with -1.39%. Peers' Q4 booking disclosures this month: Okeanis (11 Nov, after close) -1.9% the next session, Frontline (20 Nov, bmo) +2.1%, Hafnia (18 Nov) -2.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the sector's Q4 rates are public through peers, and CAPT rose 6.6% in the five sessions after Frontline's release. What is not priced is the CAPT-specific number on thin coverage (3 analysts, $3.8m/day of turnover). The Yahoo Q4 estimate implies earnings falling quarter on quarter, and the stock trades at NOK 175 against targets of NOK 226-290. If the market held a Q4 near 2x Q3, the estimates would show it. Cut for proxy transmission (peer to company), for discharge-to-discharge accounting that will print below Frontline's headline, and for the November correction weighing on the open ~30% of days.
findings.independence: Okeanis Q3 release (11 Nov): Q4 Suezmax 60% booked at $410,900/day, VLCC spot 48% at $688,800 (https://finviz.com/news/421240/okeanis-eco-tankers-corp-unaudited-condensed-financial-results-for-the-third-quarter-and-nine-month-period-of-2026). CAPT's own M/T Amor 15-month charter at about $160-180k/day (https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=685839).

findings.finding: Rates corrected sharply in early November. Kpler (6 Nov) measured Suezmax WAF-UKC down 40% in a week ($18.27 to $11.01/bbl) and Aframax USG-UKC from $20.75 to $11.71/bbl. CAPT's own prospectus (24 Nov) says 'More recently, the spot market has softened versus recent highs', so the open Q4 days and the outlook commentary carry downside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No CAPT print has carried a softening outlook. The sector fell 15-20% from 30 Oct to mid-November on the correction.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the 20-day -15.4% matches the peers' drop from the 30 Oct peak. What remains is only the chance that management's outlook makes the November softening explicit on the call. Kpler expected rates to level off and rebound, which limits it.
findings.independence: Prospectus section 10.2, 24 Nov 2026: 'More recently, the spot market has softened versus recent highs' (https://www.capitaltankers.com/files/pdf/CAPITAL_TANKERS_CORP_Prospectus.pdf). Okeanis management said rates 'had corrected from October peaks' (https://quartr.com/events/okeanis-eco-tankers-oet-q3-2026_3sH2c95u, an AI summary, snippet-grade).

findings.finding: The dividend payout is set against $1.46bn of remaining newbuild capex ($948m of it in 2027), which the prospectus says will be funded partly from operating cash flow. A Q3 payout near the Q2 ~46% (vs 90-100% at Frontline and Okeanis) is the likely outcome, which leaves the dividend line no better than neutral.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's step-up from NOK 0.50 to 3.00 was announced alongside a -1.39% day.
findings.why_not_priced: The payout policy is only 'a portion of Ordinary Net Income' (prospectus section 5.1), so the level is genuinely new on the day. The size is small because a payout around half is what the Q1-Q2 trend already shows.
findings.independence: Frontline paid out 100% of adjusted EPS ($2.38/share) and Okeanis $7.00 on $7.67 for Q3 (https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=687036 ; https://finviz.com/news/421240/okeanis-eco-tankers-corp-unaudited-condensed-financial-results-for-the-third-quarter-and-nine-month-period-of-2026).
